Counsel for Applicant :- Karunesh Pratap Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vinay Kumar Tripathi
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Karunesh Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri R.P. Patel,
learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
Learned counsel for the informant is not present.

2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 16 of 2023, under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 IPC, Police Station Nautanwa,
District Maharajganj, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

3. As per prosecution story, the applicant and other co-accused person are stated to have duped the informant on the pretext that they have extracted gold from the river and are ready to sell it to the informant and other persons.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.

Learned counsel has further stated Pramod Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39440433/

sentences.text:
that the FIR is delayed by three days and the name of the applicant has come up in the statement of the arrested co-accused person which is not admissible under the Indian Evidence Act.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents except one case in which he has been bailed out and the same stands explained vide para no. 3 of the supplementary affidavit.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.
